title: Lavorano per Guess, Calvin Klein, e Tommy Hilfiger, ma guadagnano meno di 1 dollaro al giorno
description: Il settore tessile in Etiopia – il secondo paese più popoloso dell’Africa con 105 milioni di abitanti - cresce a ritmi significativi. Il governo prevede che le esportazioni del comparto, che attualmente valgono 145 milioni di dollari l'anno, salgano a circa 30 miliardi. Un obiettivo tuttavia che appare irrealistico, se non altro perché bassi salari hanno portato a una scarsa produttività, a ripetuti scioperi e a un esasperato turn over (le fabbriche sostituiscono in media tutti i loro dipendenti ogni dodici mesi). Secondo un rapporto della New York University, i lavoratori etiopi con 26 dollari al mese sono tra i meno retribuiti al mondo. E, paradossalmente, sono dipendenti di marchi globali come Guess, H&M, Calvin Klein, Gap, Tommy Hilfiger, e JC Penney che nel paese africano hanno delocalizzato i loro stabilimenti. L'Etiopia, che mira a diventare il principale centro manifatturiero del continente, ha sedotto gli investitori facendo passare il messaggio che sarebbe stato sufficiente riconoscere ai lavoratori meno di un terzo dei salari offerti in Bangladesh. E si consideri che per lo stesso lavoro i kenyoti sono pagati 207 dollari al mese e i cinesi 326.

title: Country Representative

description: About the Company VANZBON Global is an international business services platform supporting companies and entrepreneurs with overseas market entry, company incorporation, accounting and tax compliance, legal coordination, business resource integration, and cross-border operational support. The successful candidate will assist foreign clients with company establishment, local business reception, coordination of accounting and tax-related matters, and the development of a strong local service-provider and business-resource network. This role requires strong local knowledge, excellent communication skills, and the ability to connect Ethiopia-based professional and commercial resources with VANZBON Global’s headquarters in Shenzhen, China. Coordinate with relevant government authorities, lawyers, accountants, consultants, banks, and other local service providers. Support clients in understanding local incorporation procedures, business licenses, permits, and basic compliance requirements. Help collect, prepare, coordinate, and submit necessary documents with local professional partners. Client Reception & Local Coordination Represent VANZBON Global when receiving foreign clients visiting Ethiopia. Assist with business meetings, local introductions, site visits, and communication with local stakeholders. Provide practical on-the-ground support to clients during their business establishment and operational processes. Coordinate communication between clients, local service providers, and VANZBON Global’s Shenzhen headquarters. Accounting & Tax Coordination Assist clients in connecting with qualified local accounting and tax service providers. Coordinate matters related to bookkeeping, tax registration, tax filing, payroll, social security, and other financial compliance requirements. Local Resource Development Build and maintain a reliable local partner and supplier network, including but not limited to: Law firms Accounting and audit firms Tax advisory firms Corporate service providers Banks and financial institutions Customs clearance companies Freight forwarding and logistics companies Import/export service providers Industrial parks Factories and warehouse resources Office and commercial property resources Supply-chain upstream and downstream companies HR and recruitment agencies Government and investment promotion resources Business associations and chambers of commerce Other professional and commercial service providers Resource Connection with Shenzhen Headquarters Introduce high-quality Ethiopia-based professional and commercial resources to VANZBON Global’s Shenzhen headquarters. Help evaluate the capabilities, service scope, pricing, responsiveness, and reliability of potential local partners. Coordinate cooperation discussions between VANZBON Global and local service providers. Maintain and continuously expand VANZBON Global’s local service network in Ethiopia. Business Development Support Identify potential foreign-investment opportunities and local market-entry needs. Provide basic market intelligence and updates on the Ethiopian business environment. Support VANZBON Global in identifying potential clients, partners, and cooperation opportunities. Assist with local business development activities when required. Qualifications Currently based in Ethiopia and familiar with the local business environment. Strong understanding of company registration, business operations, professional services, or foreign investment in Ethiopia. Good local network or ability to develop relationships with lawyers, accountants, tax advisors, logistics companies, industrial parks, factories, and other business service providers. Strong communication, coordination, and problem-solving skills. Able to independently follow up on client requests and local projects. Professional, reliable, responsive, and service-oriented. Comfortable working with an international team and reporting to the Shenzhen headquarters. Good command of English is required. Chinese language ability is an advantage but not required. title: Training Specialist
description: Addis Abeba, Ethiopia 611 days ago Description AndyTec is seeking a highly motivated and experienced Training Specialist to design, develop, and deliver effective training programs for employees, customers, and clients. The ideal candidate will be passionate about learning and development, with the ability to create engaging training content and help individuals enhance their technical skills in automation, control systems, and other areas related to AndyTec’s services. Requirements Education: Bachelor’s degree in Education, Instructional Design, Engineering, or a related field. Experience: 3+ years of experience in training, instructional design, or a related role, preferably in technical fields such as automation or control systems. Proven experience designing and delivering technical training programs for diverse audiences. Familiarity with learning management systems (LMS) and eLearning authoring tools (e.g., Articulate, Captivate, etc.). Skills: Strong knowledge of training methodologies, instructional design principles, and adult learning theories. Excellent communication, presentation, and facilitation skills, with the ability to engage diverse audiences. Ability to simplify complex technical concepts and deliver them in an accessible, clear, and concise manner. Proficient in using Microsoft Office and other training-related software. Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects and meet deadlines. Creative problem-solving skills and the ability to innovate in training delivery and content development. Bonuses Training Program Success Bonus: Based on positive feedback, successful completion of training initiatives, and measurable improvements in performance. Performance-Based Incentives: Annual performance reviews with opportunities for salary increases and bonuses based on individual and team achievements. Employee Engagement Bonus: Rewarded for improving employee participation, retention, and satisfaction in training programs. Benefits Competitive Salary: Based on qualifications and experience. Health & Wellness: Comprehensive health insurance and wellness programs. Retirement Savings: Access to company-sponsored retirement savings plans. Professional Development: Opportunities for further certifications, training, and career advancement. Flexible Work Schedule: Possibility of flexible working hours or remote work options. Paid Time Off: Generous vacation days, sick leave, and public holidays. Bonus & Incentives: Performance-based bonuses tied to successful training program outcomes and employee engagement. Responsibilities Training Program Development: Design, develop, and implement training programs for employees, clients, and external stakeholders on topics related to automation, control systems, process optimization, and other technical subjects. Create training materials such as manuals, guides, and eLearning content tailored to the needs of different audiences. Continuously update training materials to ensure content is accurate, relevant, and aligned with the latest industry trends and technologies. Training Delivery & Facilitation: Facilitate in-person and virtual training sessions for employees, customers, and clients. Deliver interactive and engaging presentations, demonstrations, and hands-on training to ensure a deep understanding of technical topics. Assess learner performance and provide feedback to help individuals improve their skills and knowledge. Assessment & Evaluation: Develop and administer assessments, quizzes, and tests to evaluate the effectiveness of training programs. Monitor participant progress and provide ongoing support to ensure successful completion of training. Gather feedback from trainees and adjust programs as necessary to improve training outcomes and satisfaction. Needs Analysis & Customization: Collaborate with managers, engineers, and subject matter experts to identify training needs and gaps within the organization. Customize training programs to meet the specific requirements of different teams, departments, or clients. Conduct training needs assessments to determine areas for improvement and ensure training programs align with business goals. Knowledge Transfer & Documentation: Develop a knowledge-sharing culture by creating systems for capturing and distributing training content, best practices, and lessons learned. Maintain comprehensive records of training activities, schedules, and participant progress. Prepare and distribute post-training materials and resources to reinforce learning. Continuous Improvement & Innovation: Stay up-to-date with the latest developments in training technologies, methodologies, and industry trends. Continuously improve training processes and content to enhance learner engagement and effectiveness. Participate in industry conferences, workshops, and seminars to further develop training skills and knowledge. Apply Now

description: Sales Promoter: Ethiopia Do you have a passion for agriculture and enjoy working closely with farmers and rural communities? We are looking for an energetic Sales Promoter to join our Enza Zaden Sales team in Ethiopia and support demand creation, product awareness and last-mile farmer engagement. If you are excited about promoting high-quality vegetable seeds and helping farmers access solutions that support productivity, keep reading! This is why you want to join us as Sales Promoter at Enza Zaden Meaningful work in farming communities: Play an important role in connecting farmers with high-quality vegetable varieties and practical product information at village, market and community level. Hands-on field exposure: Be part of field marketing activities, basic demonstrations and farmer engagement initiatives that bring our seed portfolio closer to growers. Opportunity to build strong relationships: Work directly with farmers, agro-dealers and local stakeholders while supporting the wider sales team with grassroots activation. Make a difference as Sales Promoter at Enza Zaden As a Sales Promoter at Enza Zaden, you will support our field marketing and demand creation activities across sales areas in Ethiopia. You will work closely with Sales Representatives to increase product awareness, support simple demonstrations and promote our seed brands at the last-mile level. In this role you will need to: Promote our products: Create product awareness in villages, markets, agro-dealer shops and community events. Engage farmers: Conduct basic farmer engagement activities and support demo plots to help growers understand product performance and benefits. Strengthen visibility: Ensure product visibility and distribute promotional materials in the relevant sales areas. Share market insights: Capture simple market observations and provide timely weekly activity reports. Support the sales team: Assist Sales Representatives with grassroots activation, farmer follow-up and local promotional activities. What You Bring As a Future Colleague Completed secondary school; an agricultural or sales-related diploma will be an advantage. Comfortable working in rural communities and engaging directly with farmers. Good communication skills in local languages; ability to communicate in English is an advantage. Ability to ride a motorbike, with a valid riding license where required. High energy, reliable, self-motivated and able to follow structured work plans. Passion for agriculture, community work and building strong relationships. Willingness to travel daily within rural sales areas and support weekend or community events during peak seasons when needed.

description: This role was posted on July 24, 2026. Please note that we will review applications on a rolling basis. The Role At Last Mile Health (LMH), we work to deploy a health worker within reach of everyone, everywhere. Do you have experience shaping health financing policy, influencing government decision-making, and building partnerships that strengthen national health systems? If so, you may be our Advisor, Health Financing with the Ethiopia program. The Advisor, Health Financing, will provide strategic technical support to the Federal Ministry of Health to strengthen sustainable financing for Ethiopia's community health system. Embedded within the Ministry's Health Strategic Affairs Department, the Advisor will support evidence-informed policymaking, advocate for increased domestic investment in the Health Extension Program (HEP), and work closely with government stakeholders to strengthen health financing policies, budget planning, and accountability mechanisms. Reporting to the Deputy Country Director, with a dotted line to the Director of Health Financing for technical mentorship, the Advisor will serve as a key liaison between the Ministry of Health (MoH), the Ministry of Finance (MoF), the Legislature, Regional and District Authorities, and development partners. Working as part of Last Mile Health's multidisciplinary Health Systems Strengthening team, the role will help ensure community health priorities are reflected in national policies, budget decisions, and long-term strategies that strengthen and sustain government-led primary health care. The role will contribute to Ethiopia’s broader efforts to strengthen primary health care (PHC) financing and support regional initiatives such as Africa Frontline First, which promotes the expansion and professionalization of community health workers across Africa. This position is a 24-month Fixed-term role with the potential of renewal. This position is only open to candidates who are currently located and authorized to work in Ethiopia. This role is onsite and located in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. What You'll Do Domestic Resource Mobilization (DRM) for Health Extension Worker Program Analyze domestic resource mobilization trends for PHC and the HEP, identifying fiscal space options at federal and regional levels Develop an investment case for sustained government financing of HEP, targeted at Federal MoH, MoF, and regional health bureaus. Conduct cross-country comparative analysis of Universal Health Coverage (UHC) performance and health financing composition among Sub-Saharan African peer countries to generate evidence for Ethiopia's DRM strategy. Convene an annual high-level advocacy event with key decision-makers to drive continuous political prioritization of community health financing. Develop an annual community health financing brief summarizing funding needs, priority investments, and expected service delivery outcomes timed to the federal budget cycle. Explore and document feasible innovative financing mechanisms for community health in the Ethiopian context. Sample and analyze several woredas to identify challenges inhibiting budget allocation to community health programs at the district /Woreda level. Participate directly (Budget advocacy) in the budget-making process at select woredas and the national level to secure budget allocations for community health programs. Build the capacity of regional and woreda health offices in budget negotiation and budget advocacy. Develop at least 2 Health Financing policy briefs or research papers for national and cross-country use. Focus on topics such as: Ethiopia’s UHC performance comparison, service delivery components contributing to UHC, health financing composition vs. peer countries, the relationship between public health expenditure and UHC, financing/policy reforms, and required resource mobilization efforts Participate in LMH cross-country convenings and contribute Ethiopian lessons to the shared learning agenda. Analyze financing gaps and inefficiencies across woredas and service delivery areas. Develop policy recommendations to improve the alignment of partner financing with national community health strategies and government planning processes. title: Senior Associate, Clinical AI
description: Overview The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc. (CHAI) is a global health organization committed to our mission of saving lives and reducing the burden of disease in low-and middle-income countries. We work at the invitation of governments to support them and the private sector to create and sustain high-quality health systems. CHAI was founded in 2002 in response to the HIV/AIDS epidemic, with the goal of dramatically reducing the price of life-saving drugs and increasing access to these medicines in the countries with the highest burden of the disease. Over the following two decades, CHAI has expanded its focus. Today, along with HIV, we work with our partners to prevent and treat infectious diseases such as COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis, and hepatitis. Our work has also expanded into cancer, diabetes, hypertension, and other non-communicable diseases, and we work to accelerate the rollout of lifesaving vaccines, reduce maternal and child mortality, combat chronic malnutrition, and increase access to assistive technology. We are investing in horizontal approaches to strengthen health systems through programs in human resources for health, digital health, and health financing. With each new and innovative program, our strategy is grounded in maximizing sustainable impact at scale, ensuring that governments lead the solutions, that programs are designed to scale nationally, and learnings are shared globally. At CHAI, our people are our greatest asset, and none of this work would be possible without their talent, time, dedication, and passion for our mission and values. We are a highly diverse team of enthusiastic individuals across 40 countries with a broad range of skill sets and life experiences. CHAI is deeply grounded in the countries we work in, with the majority of our staff based in program countries. Learn more about our exciting work: http://www.clintonhealthaccess.org CHAI is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and is committed to providing an environment of fairness, and mutual respect where all applicants have access to equal employment opportunities. CHAI values diversity and inclusion, and recognizes that our mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people with diverse experience, backgrounds, and culture. Position Overview Leveraging deep expertise in strengthening healthcare systems, CHAI has launched an ambitious Artificial Intelligence (AI) initiative that responsibly harnesses AI to radically enhance health delivery, improve patient and provider experiences, and achieve significant cost and efficiency gains in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). AI promises a significant leap in diagnostics, treatment optimization, patient engagement, and health systems efficiency. CHAI’s AI initiative seeks to systematically capture and scale these benefits, delivering meaningful, sustainable health impacts at scale. CHAI is seeking an Associate or Senior Associate, Clinical AI to contribute to Clinical AI implementation work in Ethiopia. The successful candidate is a practicing or recently practicing clinician — medical doctor, nurse, or midwife — who brings real-world clinical workflow, user needs, and implementation realities into the design, evaluation, and rollout of the initiative’s AI-powered tools. Reporting to the Sr Manager, AI (Ethiopia), and working closely with CHAI’s Global Clinical AI team, this role is the clinical and implementation engine of the country-level work. This Clinical AI role for Ethiopia is responsible for scoping clinical and user requirements from the country’s clinical context — workflow, clinical practice, connectivity, interoperability, infrastructure — and feeding them with precision into the global product and engineering process. The role will drive product clinical stakeholder engagement, scoping, evaluation coordination, and implementation in country. The work moves quickly. The team requires someone who can absorb new contexts fast, surface concerns and solutions constructively, provide defensible critique, push for precision without slowing the pace, and gel naturally with both country and global colleagues. The information this role gathers — clinical scenarios, workflow steps, edge cases, evaluation findings — is what the models and products will be built on; accuracy and traceability are non-negotiable. Likewise, the post holder will be responsible for generating this information with impeccable respect for patient privacy, informed consent, research ethics, and data governance. This position is based in Ethiopia. Position levelling is flexible and commensurate with the successful performance of the candidate and their experience; the role may be filled at the Associate or Senior Associate level. The role requires regular travel within the country and some international travel (10–25% annually). title: SCS Project Health Program Supply Chain Advisor for HIV/AIDS and TB
description: Main Purpose Of Job The Health Program Supply Chain advisor for HIV/AIDS and TB, embedded within the Ministry of Health’s Pharmaceutical and Medical Devices Lead Executive Office (PMD LEO), provides technical assistance in demand planning, resource mobilization, procurement, stock status and pipeline monitoring, and overall supply chain management of HIV/AIDS and TB program commodities. Work with public and private sector partners to implement HIV/AIDS and TB supply chain activities across the country, ensuring alignment with national health program strategies. Collaborate with the SCS team, MOH, EPSS, and other key stakeholders to design and implement supply chain strengthening strategies, tools, and approaches to improve HIV and TB commodity availability while conducting and supporting supply management assessments to evaluate and enhance supply chain operations. title: Senior Non-Key Expert – IT Audit (SNKE – Audit 9)
description: For Project: Service Contract for Technical Facility Unit (TFU) for the EU Support to Public Finance Management Reforms in Ethiopia (EUSPRE) The European Union is supporting the Government of Ethiopia through the EUSPRE public financial management (PFM) project. The EUSPRE Technical Facility Unit (TFU) provides oversight of the EUSPRE programme and specifically support and capacity building support to the Federal government’s PFM Reforms program. The Overall Objective of the EUSPRE programme is enhanced transparency and efficiency of public financial management for better service delivery and inclusive development . DAI is looking for a Senior Non-Key Expert – IT Audit (SNKE – Audit 9) to Support the Office of the Federal Auditor General (OFAG) by updating the current IT Audit Manual and Working Papers and delivering related Dissemination Workshop and Classroom Training. Scope of work The scope of work for this assignment includes the following activities/ tasks to be undertaken by the NKE, in conjunction with the OFAG designated working group led by the Director of ITAU, which are further detailed in the two sub-sections below: 1. Carry out consultations with the KE3 (TFU) and the OFAG designated working group led by Director of ITAU, and assessment of the scope of work. Review already prepared/approved Gap Analysis related to areas of manual requiring update in conjunction with KE3 (TFU) and the OFAG designated working group led by Director of ITAU. 3. Support updating of the OFAG IT Audit Manual (Version 2018) and respective Working Papers, as agreed during the inception meetings, and in line with the approved changes set within Gap Analysis, taking in consideration necessary customisation to the Ethiopian context. 4. Develop dissemination workshop materials for the updated version of IT Audit Manual and WPs, facilitate and deliver a one-day Dissemination Workshop for the Senior Management (total 40 attendees). The workshop will be a ‘kick-start’ to establish arrangements for adoption and rollout for the updated version of the OFAG IT Audit Manual (Version 2026) and respective Working Papers. 5. Develop two training modules (materials) for Classroom Trainings on the updated OFAG IT Audit Manual and WPs (Version 2026) and new IT Audit practices practical for the ITAU Director and Auditors, FADs and P&ED Directors and Managers, AQAD and T&ED teams members (total 40 participants). 6. Facilitate and deliver training over two one-week training sessions (five days each, total ten days). First week (Module 1) is going to be delivered to 30 participants comprised of staff from ITAU and selected staff from: FADs, P&ED, AQAD and T&ED; while second week (Module 2) is going to be delivered to 10 participants referring to staff from ITAU (total 40 participants). Classroom Trainings will comprise of two training modules (materials) covering following: I. Module 1 will cover a detailed presentation of updated OFAG’s IT Audit Manual and WPs (Version 2026): § An Introduction to updated OFAG’s IT Audit Manual & WPs (Version 2026) covering: a. In-depth description and elaboration of the IT Audit Manual content: Introduction, Establishing IT Audit Function, IT Audit Standards, Frameworks and Audit Work, Planning Process, Conducting the Audit, Reporting, Follow-up, Communication, Quality Control. b. In-depth description and elaboration of the WPs content. II. Module 2 will cover practical exercises relating to the application of updated OFAG’s IT Audit Manual and WPs (Version 2026) using IT Audit Case Study. The case study should cover all of the following topics, as agreed with OFAG Management: § An introduction to new working practices using IT Audit Case Study in form of classroom exercise as part of practical application of updated OFAG’s IT Audit Manual and WPs (Version 2026) in the following areas: Audit of IT Governance and Segregation of Duties; Audit of Network and Systems (Hardware & Software); Audit of Active Directory and other User Management Systems; Audit of IT Security and Cybersecurity Areas; Audit of Data Centres and it’s Environment; Audit of ERP Applications and Databases; Audit of Backup Solutions and Disaster Recovery; Audit of AI and Emerging Technologies (Cloud Computing, IoT, Big Data, etc.); Audit of IT Projects and Systems under Development. 7. Prepare combined end-of-assignment report reflecting on the work delivered for updating of the OFAG IT Audit Manual (Version 2026) and respective Working Papers as well as for delivery of Dissemination Workshop and delivery of Classroom Trainings. title: Digital Identity Lead - Frontier Technologies Foundations
description: The Digital Identity Lead is a high-visibility, dual-engine role sitting at the intersection of technical architecture and commercial origination. The role's anchor specialism is Digital Identity (DID): you will bring deep, hands-on experience of building or implementing national-scale digital identity architectures, and you will ultimately own FT's DID service line. Because identity is a load-bearing foundation beneath the rest of FT's foundations stack — every national data ecosystem depends on a trusted unique identifier, and every identity system depends on a cryptographic trust and security layer — this role is deliberately broader than a pure DID mandate. You will carry contributory technical responsibility into Data at Societal Scale (national data exchange, interoperability, data governance) and Cybersecurity (PKI, cryptographic trust frameworks, Zero Trust design), acting as FT's connective thread across these three foundations. You will not be expected to lead these adjacent domains, but to ensure DID engagements are architected coherently with them, and to lend specialist input when FT's Data and Cyber leads need identity-layer expertise. You will also act as a core business builder for the practice, using your global network within the World Bank, the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, and the broader DPI ecosystem to originate new projects, secure funding, and scale Genesis's pipeline across all three foundations. 1 | Key Responsibilities 1.1 Business Origination & Strategic Networks (35%) Pipeline Generation: Leverage existing, high-level relationships within the World Bank, Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation (BMGF), Co-Develop, and key regional development banks to position Genesis as the premier global choice for DPI implementation — opening doors for Data at Societal Scale and Cybersecurity mandates as a natural extension of DID relationships Deal Structuring & Capture: Proactively identify, shape, and capture business opportunities across the DID and foundational ID ecosystem; lead high-value proposal development and pitches for donor-funded tenders, and contribute technical input to Data and Cybersecurity pursuits where identity is a component Ecosystem Integration: Act as a primary interface between Genesis and the global identity, data, and digital government communities, aligning firm capabilities with emerging donor strategies, funding cycles, and country-level roadmaps 1.2 Digital Identity — Technical Leadership & Implementation (35%) National-Scale Delivery: Serve as the chief subject-matter expert on the architectural design, governance, and roll-out strategies of foundational or functional national digital ID systems Framework Champion: Embed international standards and best practice — specifically World Bank ID4D principles, ID4Africa frameworks, and open-source stacks such as MOSIP — into localised government roadmaps Next-Gen Identity Architecture: Advise clients on the transition toward Decentralised Identity (DID) ecosystems, Verifiable Credentials (VCs), and self-sovereign identity (SSI) frameworks Cross-Functional Integration: Ensure identity frameworks interoperate seamlessly with the other DPI pillars — payments, data exchange, and (in time) national cybersecurity architecture 1.3 Contributory Technical Leadership: Data & Cybersecurity Foundations (20%) Data at Societal Scale: Advise on how unique identifiers and civil registries underpin national data exchange and interoperability architecture; contribute an identity lens to national data strategy and data governance engagements led by FT's Data practice Cybersecurity: Bring your natural DID-adjacent expertise in cryptographic trust frameworks, PKI, and public/private key infrastructure to inform Zero Trust architecture, authentication and authorisation design, and identity-linked security posture assessments — supporting the build-out of FT's cybersecurity service line ahead of its 2027 launch Coherence Across Foundations: Act as the technical bridge ensuring DID, Data, and Cybersecurity workstreams are designed as one interoperable stack rather than three siloed engagements, in line with FT's GOAT framework (Governance, Operations, Adoption, Technology) 1.4 Practice Building & Thought Leadership (10%) Mentorship: Guide and upskill a growing team of consultants and analysts across FT's foundations pillar, fostering a culture of technical excellence beyond DID alone Global Presence: Represent Genesis at premier international forums — ID4Africa, World Bank Digital Government and Spring Meetings, and DID/data/cyber developer convenings — publishing high-impact insights and whitepapers that span the foundations stack How This Role Differs From a Pure DID Mandate Anchor specialism: Digital Identity — full ownership, national-scale delivery track record required Contributory remit: Data at Societal Scale and Cybersecurity — working fluency and cross-practice coordination, not delivery ownership Why broadened: Identity is the found

description: Job Description Introduction Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Its protection interventions in Ethiopia follow a six-pillar intervention that includes direct assistance to migrants, displaced persons and affected communities, thematic guidance, capacity development, advocacy, and research. The Protection Unit (PXU) works closely with the government of Ethiopia and various stakeholders in emergency, displacement, and migration settings to reduce protection risks and address the needs of vulnerable individuals and communities. Additionally, the selected candidate will support the team in trainings and capacity building related to specialized protection, TiP and SoM, and other topics related to provision of assistance to vulnerable migrants. The selected candidate will also be required to provide additional support, as necessary, to other protection teams, including the Return and Reintegration teams, Protection Emergencies, Policy and Liaison, and to coordinate with other programmatic units in the mission.
